sheet-1-1.description: The first part of sheet 1 lies below and to the right of the heavy dividing lines under the key map, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north at the top. It shows East Main from about lot 214 east to lot 270 at the eastern end of Columbus, with a 6 inch water pipe in the street, and at its right Cherry running north from East Main to meet Locust Avenue (Ridgeway Avenue), which comes in diagonally from the west. Both sides of East Main are lined with frame dwellings, most of two stories, with sheds, auto houses and stables behind them in blocks 1, 2 and 6; a brick-fronted dwelling stands on the south side, and a hall stands north of East Main west of Cherry. Five small dwellings face Cherry in block 16, and fire hydrants are marked along East Main. The ground beyond is marked no exposure.
notes: Cherry is today's Cherry Lane; East Main east of Cherry continues as Mount Pleasant Road.
Placed from the Cherry / East Main junction (detected), a hand-picked Cherry / Locust Avenue point and a point derived 300 ft west along East Main; low confidence.

sheet-1-2.description: The second part of sheet 1 is the band between the two heavy dividing lines below the key map, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north at the top but at a different angle from the rest of the sheet. It shows New York Avenue (Water) running north from Locust Avenue (Ridgeway Avenue), with a 6 inch water pipe, between blocks 1, 2 and 3. Frame dwellings with stables and sheds line the west side of New York Avenue, and the Charles Hankins sash and blind factory, powered by a gasoline engine and without heat or fire apparatus, stands at the left. East of the avenue the large block 1 holds a few dwellings and a two-story auto house; most of it, and the ground beyond, is open or marked no exposure.
notes: Placed on the single junction New York Avenue / Locust Avenue with an assumed scale (8.0 px/ft) and the rotation of the measured lines; low confidence.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the centre of Columbus at 50 feet to an inch, where West Main and East Main cross New York Avenue (Water), running north, and Atlantic Avenue (Pine), running south; Locust Avenue (Ridgeway Avenue) crosses the top of the sheet. Around the crossroads stand the Columbus Hotel with its hitching sheds, two concrete-block garages, John Sharp's carriage and auto repair shop with lumber storage and a paint shop, stores and a private garage. Public buildings include the Columbus Public School on Locust Avenue, the Town Hall and the Franklin Fire Co. on Atlantic Avenue, the I.O.O.F. Hall, the Wesley M.E. Church on East Main and the P.O. Baptist Church. Sales stables and a horse shed lie off Atlantic Avenue. Elsewhere the blocks hold frame dwellings, several brick ones, and outbuildings. Water pipes run in the main streets and fire hydrants are marked.
notes: West Main is today's Columbus Road; East Main is East Main Street.
Placed from two junctions only (Main / New York / Atlantic and New York / Locust; helmert); low confidence away from New York Avenue.

50 ft. Village centre: Main Street at New York Avenue (Water) and Atlantic Avenue (Pine), Locust Avenue (Ridgeway Avenue) at the top; Columbus Hotel, Public School, Town Hall, Franklin Fire Co, Wesley M.E. Church, P.O. Baptist Church, John Sharp carriage shop. One part.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers West Main west of the centre of Columbus at 50 feet to an inch, turned so that north is to the upper left. West Main runs diagonally across the sheet; Hedding Avenue (Hadding Avenue) leaves it to the north-west and Railroad Avenue (Pennsylvania Avenue) to the south-east. The P.R.R. Amboy Division Kinkora Branch crosses West Main on a stone bridge between them, with sidings serving the Century Milk Co. creamery, a hay and feed building and storage sheds. St. Luke's Protestant Episcopal Church stands on the north side of West Main and the Baptist Church, with a long horse shed, on the south side. The rest of the sheet is frame dwellings with outbuildings, an ice house and a few brick dwellings; water pipes run in West Main.
notes: West Main is today's Columbus Road; Hedding Avenue matches today's Mill Lane West at its south end (its modern junction with Columbus Road is about 17 m from the drawn one and was not used).
The Kinkora Branch is abandoned; OpenStreetMap does not map it through the village.
Placed on Columbus Road / Railroad Avenue (hand-picked) and a point derived 300 ft west along West Main; low confidence.

50 ft. West Main west of the centre, Hedding Avenue (Hadding Avenue), Railroad Avenue (Pennsylvania Avenue), P.R.R. Amboy Division Kinkora Branch crossing Main at a stone bridge; Century Milk Co, St. Luke's Episcopal Church, Baptist Church. One part, north to the upper left.
